learn.b: नमस्ते (namaste) means hello. अलविदा (alvidā) means goodbye. Both are polite and common.
धन्यवाद (dhanyavād) means thank you. शुक्रिया (shukriyā) is a friendly way to say thanks. माफ़ कीजिए (māf kījiye) means excuse me or sorry.
हाँ (hāṃ) means yes and नहीं (nahīṃ) means no. Say मेरा नाम रवि है (merā nām Ravi hai) for My name is Ravi.

learn.b: मैं (maiṃ) is I and तुम (tum) is you. हूँ (hūṃ) is am and है (hai) is is. मैं छात्र हूँ (maiṃ chhātra hūṃ) means I am a student.
क्या (kyā) at the start makes a yes or no question. It also means what. कहाँ (kahāṃ) means where.
जाना (jānā) means to go and आना (ānā) means to come. स्कूल (skūl) means school. मेरे पास एक बिल्ली है (mere pās ek billī hai) means I have a cat.

qs.q: What does क्या (kyā) mean at the start of a sentence?
qs.why: क्या (kyā) starts a yes or no question and also means what.

qs.q: How do you say 'I am a student'?
qs.why: हूँ (hūṃ) goes with मैं (maiṃ) and means am.

qs.q: What does कहाँ (kahāṃ) mean?
How do you say 'I have a cat'?
o: मैं एक बिल्ली हूँ (maiṃ ek billī hūṃ)
मेरे पास एक बिल्ली है (mere pās ek billī hai)
मैं बिल्ली जाता हूँ (maiṃ billī jātā hūṃ)
qs.why: मेरे पास (mere pās) is the way to say I have.

qs.q: है (hai) means 'is'.
qs.why: है (hai) is the present tense of to be for he, she, and it.

learn.b: क्या (kyā) means what. कौन (kaun) means who. कहाँ (kahāṃ) means where. आप कौन हैं? (āp kaun haiṃ) means Who are you?
कब (kab) means when. क्यों (kyoṃ) means why. कैसे (kaise) means how. कितना (kitnā) means how much or how many.
आपका नाम क्या है? (āpkā nām kyā hai) means What is your name? आप कैसे हैं? (āp kaise haiṃ) means How are you?

qs.why: नाम (nām) is name and क्या (kyā) is what.

learn.b: लाल (lāl) is red. नीला (nīlā) is blue. हरा (harā) is green. पीला (pīlā) is yellow. काला (kālā) is black. सफ़ेद (safed) is white.
बड़ा (baṛā) means big and छोटा (chhoṭā) means small. अच्छा (achchhā) means good and बुरा (burā) means bad. नया (nayā) is new and पुराना (purānā) is old.
The adjective comes before the noun. बड़ा घर (baṛā ghar) is a big house. For a girl or woman, -ā changes to -ī: बड़ी लड़की (baṛī laṛkī). मुझे नीला पसंद है (mujhe nīlā pasand hai) means I like blue.

qs.q: What does लाल (lāl) mean?
How do you say 'a big house'?
How do you say 'a big girl'?
qs.why: With a girl, बड़ा (baṛā) becomes बड़ी (baṛī).

qs.q: Which word means 'white'?
qs.why: सफ़ेद (safed) is white and काला (kālā) is black.

qs.q: पुराना (purānā) means new.
qs.why: पुराना (purānā) means old. New is नया (nayā).

learn.b: सोमवार (somvār) is Monday, मंगलवार (maṅgalvār) is Tuesday, बुधवार (budhvār) is Wednesday, गुरुवार (guruvār) is Thursday. शुक्रवार (shukravār) is Friday, शनिवार (shanivār) is Saturday, रविवार (ravivār) is Sunday.
सुबह (subah) is morning, दोपहर (dopahar) is afternoon, शाम (shām) is evening and रात (rāt) is night. आज रविवार है (āj ravivār hai) means Today is Sunday.
बजे (baje) means o'clock. तीन बजे (tīn baje) means at three o'clock. अभी क्या समय है? (abhī kyā samay hai) means What time is it now?

में (meṃ) means in. कमरे में एक मेज़ है (kamre meṃ ek mez hai) means There is a table in the room. मेरा (merā) means my and तुम्हारा (tumhārā) means your.

learn.b: Add -ता (-tā) to the verb stem, then हूँ (hūṃ). मैं जाता हूँ (maiṃ jātā hūṃ) means I go. A woman says -ती: मैं जाती हूँ (maiṃ jātī hūṃ).
उठना (uṭhnā) is to get up, नहाना (nahānā) is to bathe, पढ़ना (paṛhnā) is to read or study, सोना (sonā) is to sleep. मैं सोता हूँ (maiṃ sotā hūṃ) means I sleep.
रोज़ (roz) means every day. हमेशा (hamesha) means always. कभी-कभी (kabhī-kabhī) means sometimes. मैं रोज़ स्कूल जाता हूँ (maiṃ roz skūl jātā hūṃ) means I go to school every day.

qs.why: रोज़ (roz) is every day and जाता हूँ (jātā hūṃ) is I go.

learn.b: मौसम (mausam) is weather. बारिश (bārish) is rain, धूप (dhūp) is sunshine, हवा (havā) is wind and बर्फ़ (barf) is snow. गरमी (garmī) is heat and सर्दी (sardī) is cold.
आज मौसम अच्छा है (āj mausam achchhā hai) means Today the weather is good. बारिश हो रही है (bārish ho rahī hai) means It is raining.
कपड़े (kapṛe) means clothes. कमीज़ (kamīz) is shirt, जूते (jūte) are shoes and टोपी (ṭopī) is hat. मैं टोपी पहनता हूँ (maiṃ ṭopī pahantā hūṃ) means I wear a hat.

learn.b: गया (gayā) means went and खाया (khāyā) means ate. मैं स्कूल गया (maiṃ skūl gayā) means I went to school. था (thā) means was.
Put नहीं (nahīṃ) before the past verb. मैं नहीं गया (maiṃ nahīṃ gayā) means I did not go.
आज (āj) means today and अभी (abhī) means now. पिछले हफ़्ते (pichhle hafte) means last week. कल (kal) means both yesterday and tomorrow, so the verb tells you which one.

qs.q: How do you say 'I ate food'?
o: मैं खाना नहीं हूँ (maiṃ khānā nahīṃ hūṃ)
मैं खाना पीता हूँ (maiṃ khānā pītā hūṃ)
qs.why: खाया (khāyā) is the past of eat.

qs.q: How do you say 'I went to school'?
What does था (thā) mean?
qs.why: था (thā) is the past of to be.

qs.q: How do you say 'I did not go'?
qs.why: नहीं (nahīṃ) before the past verb makes it negative.

qs.q: कल (kal) can mean both 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow'.
qs.why: Hindi uses the same word कल (kal) for both, and the verb tense shows which.

learn.b: Add -ūṅgā, -oge, -egā to the verb stem. मैं जाऊँगा (maiṃ jāūṅgā) means I will go. A woman says जाऊँगी (jāūṅgī). तुम जाओगे (tum jāoge) is you will go and वह जाएगा (vah jāegā) is he will go.
Put नहीं (nahīṃ) before the verb: मैं नहीं जाऊँगा (maiṃ nahīṃ jāūṅgā) means I will not go. कल (kal) means tomorrow here. अगले हफ़्ते (agle hafte) means next week.
मैं कल फ़िल्म देखूँगा (maiṃ kal film dekhūṅgā) means I will watch a film tomorrow. हम खाना खाएँगे (ham khānā khāeṅge) means we will eat food.

qs.q: How does a man say 'I will go'?
qs.why: मैं जाऊँगा (maiṃ jāūṅgā) is the future.

qs.q: How does a woman say 'I will go'?
qs.why: A woman uses -ī at the end.

qs.q: What does अगले हफ़्ते (agle hafte) mean?
Which sentence means 'I will not go'?
o: मैं जाऊँगा नहीं गया (maiṃ jāūṅgā nahīṃ gayā)
मैं जा रहा हूँ (maiṃ jā rahā hūṃ)
qs.why: नहीं (nahīṃ) goes before the future verb.

qs.q: तुम जाओगे (tum jāoge) means you will go.
qs.why: -oge is the future ending for तुम (tum).

दाएँ (dāeṃ) is right and बाएँ (bāeṃ) is left. सीधे (sīdhe) means straight. मुड़िए (muṛiye) means please turn.
स्टेशन (sṭeshan) is station, अस्पताल (aspatāl) is hospital, and बैंक (baiṅk) is bank. पास (pās) means near and दूर (dūr) means far.

learn.b: कितने का है (kitne kā hai) means How much is it? महँगा (mahaṅgā) means expensive and सस्ता (sastā) means cheap.
टिकट (ṭikaṭ) is ticket, होटल (hoṭal) is hotel, and पासपोर्ट (pāsporṭ) is passport. ट्रेन (ṭren) is train and यात्रा (yātrā) means journey.
Say मुझे ... चाहिए (mujhe ... chāhiye) for I need or want. मुझे एक टिकट चाहिए (mujhe ek ṭikaṭ chāhiye) means I need a ticket.

मैं एक टिकट खाता हूँ (maiṃ ek ṭikaṭ khātā hūṃ)
qs.why: मुझे ... चाहिए (mujhe ... chāhiye) means I need.

qs.q: सस्ता (sastā) means expensive.

learn.b: सिर (sir) is head, आँख (āṅkh) is eye, कान (kān) is ear, नाक (nāk) is nose and मुँह (muṅh) is mouth. हाथ (hāth) is hand, पैर (pair) is foot and पेट (peṭ) is stomach.
दर्द (dard) means pain. बुखार (bukhār) means fever. मेरे सिर में दर्द है (mere sir meṃ dard hai) means I have a headache. मुझे बुखार है (mujhe bukhār hai) means I have a fever.
डॉक्टर (ḍākṭar) is doctor, दवा (davā) is medicine and बीमार (bīmār) is sick. मुझे डॉक्टर के पास जाना है (mujhe ḍākṭar ke pās jānā hai) means I need to go to the doctor.

qs.q: What does बुखार (bukhār) mean?

मेरे पेट में दर्द है (mere peṭ meṃ dard hai)
qs.why: सिर (sir) is head and दर्द (dard) is pain.

आँख (āṅkh) means ear.
qs.why: आँख (āṅkh) means eye. Ear is कान (kān).

qs.q: Match each body word to its meaning

learn.b: डॉक्टर (ḍākṭar) is doctor, शिक्षक (shikṣak) is teacher and किसान (kisān) is farmer. इंजीनियर (injīniyar) is engineer and दुकानदार (dukāndār) is shopkeeper.
काम (kām) means work and नौकरी (naukarī) means job. आप क्या काम करते हैं? (āp kyā kām karte haiṃ) means What work do you do? Answer: मैं शिक्षक हूँ (maiṃ shikṣak hūṃ).
दफ़्तर (daftar) means office. मैं एक दफ़्तर में काम करता हूँ (maiṃ ek daftar meṃ kām kartā hūṃ) means I work in an office.

qs.q: What does शिक्षक (shikṣak) mean?
What does किसान (kisān) mean?
Which question means 'What work do you do?'
o: आप कहाँ रहते हैं? (āp kahāṃ rahte haiṃ)
आपका नाम क्या है? (āpkā nām kyā hai)
आप क्या काम करते हैं? (āp kyā kām karte haiṃ)

qs.q: What does दफ़्तर (daftar) mean?
नौकरी (naukarī) means job.
Match each job to its meaning
Put the words in order: What work do you do?

Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'job'.

lab.hint: A place where people work at desks.

learn.b: शौक़ (shauq) means hobby. खेलना (khelnā) is to play, तैरना (tairnā) is to swim, घूमना (ghūmnā) is to walk around, फ़िल्म देखना (film dekhnā) is to watch a film.

Say मुझे ... पसंद है (mujhe ... pasand hai). मुझे क्रिकेट खेलना पसंद है (mujhe cricket khelnā pasand hai) means I like playing cricket. तुम्हारा शौक़ क्या है? (tumhārā shauq kyā hai) means What is your hobby?
ख़ाली समय में (khālī samay meṃ) means in free time. अक्सर (aksar) means often and कभी नहीं (kabhī nahīṃ) means never.

qs.q: What does शौक़ (shauq) mean?
What does तैरना (tairnā) mean?
How do you say 'I like playing cricket'?
o: मैं क्रिकेट नहीं खेलता (maiṃ cricket nahīṃ kheltā)
मुझे क्रिकेट खेलना पसंद है (mujhe cricket khelnā pasand hai)

qs.q: What does कभी नहीं (kabhī nahīṃ) mean?
अक्सर (aksar) means often.
Match each Hindi word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I like playing cricket.

lab.q: Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'hobby' (Devanagari or romanized).
Challenge: type the Hindi verb meaning 'to swim'.
Challenge: what does अक्सर (aksar) mean in English?
lab.hint: It is between always and sometimes.

learn.b: मज़ेदार (mazedār) means fun and उबाऊ (ubāū) means boring. आसान (āsān) means easy and मुश्किल (mushkil) means difficult.
मुझे लगता है (mujhe lagtā hai) means I think or I feel. मुझे हिंदी पसंद है (mujhe hindī pasand hai) means I like Hindi.
क्यों (kyoṃ) means why and क्योंकि (kyoṃki) means because. लेकिन (lekin) means but.

qs.q: What does क्यों (kyoṃ) mean?
What does क्योंकि (kyoṃki) mean?
What does आसान (āsān) mean?
How do you say 'I like Hindi'?
o: मुझे हिंदी कहाँ है (mujhe hindī kahāṃ hai)
मुझे हिंदी पसंद है (mujhe hindī pasand hai)

qs.q: लेकिन (lekin) means 'but'.
Match each describing word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I think Hindi is fun

lab.q: Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'because'.
lab.hint: It sounds like क्यों plus कि.

lab.q: Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'but'.
Challenge: what does आसान (āsān) mean in English?

learn.b: से (se) means than. ज़्यादा (zyādā) means more and कम (kam) means less. हाथी चूहे से बड़ा है (hāthī chūhe se baṛā hai) means The elephant is bigger than the mouse.
सबसे (sabse) means most or the -est. चीता सबसे तेज़ जानवर है (chītā sabse tez jānvar hai) means The cheetah is the fastest animal. तेज़ (tez) is fast and धीरे (dhīre) is slow.
बराबर (barābar) means equal. यह उसके बराबर है (yah uske barābar hai) means This is equal to that.

qs.q: What does से (se) mean in a comparison?
What does सबसे (sabse) mean?
How do you say 'The elephant is bigger than the mouse'?
o: चूहा हाथी से बड़ा है (chūhā hāthī se baṛā hai)
हाथी सबसे छोटा है (hāthī sabse chhoṭā hai)
हाथी चूहे से बड़ा है (hāthī chūhe se baṛā hai)
हाथी और चूहा है (hāthī aur chūhā hai)
qs.why: से (se) goes after the thing you compare to.

qs.q: What does तेज़ (tez) mean?
बराबर (barābar) means equal.
Match each Hindi word to its meaning
Put the words in order: The elephant is bigger than the mouse.

lab.q: Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'than' (Devanagari or romanized).
lab.hint: A tiny word with two letters.

lab.q: Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'most' (as in the fastest).
Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'fast'.

learn.b: चाहिए (chāhiye) means should or need. तुम्हें आराम करना चाहिए (tumheṃ ārām karnā chāhiye) means You should rest. आराम (ārām) means rest.
अगर (agar) means if and तो (to) means then. अगर बारिश होगी तो मैं घर पर रहूँगा (agar bārish hogī to maiṃ ghar par rahūṅgā) means If it rains, I will stay at home.
शायद (shāyad) means maybe. ज़रूर (zarūr) means certainly. ज़रूरी (zarūrī) means necessary.

qs.q: What does अगर (agar) mean?
What does शायद (shāyad) mean?
How do you say 'You should rest'?
o: तुम आराम करते हो (tum ārām karte ho)
तुम्हें आराम करना चाहिए (tumheṃ ārām karnā chāhiye)
तुम्हें आराम नहीं है (tumheṃ ārām nahīṃ hai)

qs.q: What does ज़रूर (zarūr) mean?
तो (to) can mean 'then' in an if-sentence.
qs.why: अगर ... तो ... (agar ... to ...) means if ... then ...

qs.q: Match each Hindi word to its meaning
Put the words in order: If it rains...

lab.q: Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'if' (Devanagari or romanized).
Challenge: type the Hindi word for 'maybe'.
Challenge: fill in the missing word: तुम्हें आराम करना ___ (You should rest).

learn.b: Say Hello or Hi when you meet someone. Say Good morning before noon and Good evening at night. Say Goodbye when you leave.
Say Please when you ask for something. Say Thank you when someone helps you. The answer is You're welcome. Say Sorry after a mistake.
Say My name is Ana. Then say Nice to meet you. To ask how someone is, say How are you? A common answer is I'm fine, thanks.

qs.q: Which greeting do you use in the morning?
qs.why: Good morning is the greeting for the morning.

qs.q: Someone says 'Thank you.' What do you answer?
qs.why: You're welcome is the polite answer to thank you.

qs.q: How do you tell someone your name?
qs.why: My name is ... is the standard way to give your name.

qs.q: Which word makes a request polite?
You say 'Goodbye' when you leave.
qs.why: Goodbye is used when you are leaving.

qs.q: Match each phrase to when you use it
Put this short conversation in order

lab.hint: It is what you are called.
lab.why: My name is Anna introduces yourself.

lab.q: Challenge: what is the opposite of 'hello' when you leave?
lab.hint: You say it when you go.
lab.why: Goodbye is what we say when we leave.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: ___ you! (after someone gives you a gift)
lab.why: Thank you is the polite way to show you are grateful.

learn.b: The numbers are one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten. We write them as 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10.
Your mother and father are your parents. Your brother is a boy in your family and your sister is a girl in your family. Family means the people who are related to you.
Say I have two brothers. For more than one, add s: one brother, two brothers. Use have with I, you, we, and they.

qs.q: Which number is 'seven'?
Your father's wife is usually your ...
qs.why: Your father's wife is usually your mother.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ two sisters.
What is the plural of 'brother'?
qs.why: Add s to make most nouns plural.

qs.q: 'Sister' is a male family member.
qs.why: A sister is a female family member.

qs.q: Match each number word to its number
Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest

lab.q: Challenge: write the word for 3 + 4.
Challenge: complete: Your mother's mother is your ___.
lab.hint: A family word starting with grand.
lab.why: Your mother's mother is your grandmother.

lab.q: Challenge: write the word for 6 + 4.

learn.b: Breakfast is the morning meal. Lunch is the meal in the middle of the day. Dinner is the evening meal. A snack is a small bite between meals.
Common foods are bread, rice, and apples. Common drinks are water and milk. We eat food and we drink drinks.
To order politely, say I'd like some tea, please. To say what you enjoy, say I like pizza. To say the opposite, say I don't like fish.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ water every day.
qs.why: We drink water. We eat food.

qs.q: Which sentence is a polite way to order?
qs.why: I'd like ..., please is a polite way to order.

qs.q: Which meal do you eat in the morning?
qs.why: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

qs.q: Which of these is a fruit?
'Delicious' means the food tastes very good.
Match each word to its meaning
Put the words in order to make a sentence

lab.q: Challenge: complete: A white drink from cows is ___.
lab.hint: You can put it in cereal.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Breakfast, lunch and ___.
lab.hint: The last meal of the day.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: I'd like a glass of ___. (a clear drink)

learn.b: Use am with I, is with he, she, and it, and are with you, we, and they. For example: I am a student. She is a teacher.
Use have with I, you, we, and they. Use has with he, she, and it. For daily actions, add s for he, she, and it: He goes to school.
Use don't with I, you, we, and they. Use doesn't with he, she, and it. For example: I don't like fish. She doesn't eat meat.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: She ___ a student.
Choose the correct word: They ___ a dog.
Choose the correct word: He ___ to school every day.
qs.why: Add es to go for he, she, and it.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ like fish.
'He have a cat' is a correct sentence.
qs.why: It should be 'He has a cat.'

qs.q: Match each pronoun to the correct verb
Put the words in order to make a sentence

lab.q: Challenge: complete: I ___ a student. (be)
lab.why: I am is the correct form.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: She ___ a dog. (have)
lab.why: She has is the correct form.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: He ___ like fish. (negative)
lab.why: He does not like fish is the negative.

learn.b: Red, blue, green, yellow, black and white are colors. The sky is blue. Grass is green. A banana is yellow.
Big and small, hot and cold, new and old, happy and sad are describing words. They are adjectives.
An adjective comes before the noun: a red car. After is or are it comes after: The car is red. Adjectives never add -s: two red cars.

qs.q: Which sentence is correct?
qs.why: The adjective goes before the noun.

qs.q: What color is a banana?
What is the opposite of 'hot'?
Choose the correct plural: 'two ___ cars'
In English, we say 'a car red'.
qs.why: The adjective comes before the noun: a red car.

qs.q: Match each word to its opposite
Put the words in order

lab.q: Challenge: what color is the sky on a sunny day?
lab.hint: It is also the color of the sea.
lab.why: The sky is blue on a sunny day.

lab.q: Challenge: write the opposite of 'big'.
lab.why: The opposite of big is small.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: The sun is ___. (a bright color like a banana)

learn.b: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. There are seven days in a week. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.
January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December. There are twelve months in a year.
Say It's three o'clock. Use on with days (on Monday), in with months (in July) and at with time (at five o'clock).

qs.q: Which day comes after Monday?
Which month comes after March?
Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the correct sentence.
There are seven days in a week.
Match each word to its meaning
Put the days in order, starting with Monday

Challenge: how many months are there in a year? (write the word or number)

units.title: Home and Places in a House

learn.b: A house has a kitchen, a bedroom, a bathroom and a living room. You cook in the kitchen and sleep in the bedroom.
A table, a chair, a bed and a sofa are furniture. There is a lamp on the table.
In, on, under, next to and behind say where something is. The cat is under the table. The book is on the chair.

qs.q: Where do you sleep?
Where do you usually cook?
The cat is under the table. Where is the cat?
Choose the correct sentence.
o: There is a book in the chair.
There are a book on the chair.
There is a book on the chair.
qs.why: Use there is with one thing.

qs.q: A sofa is furniture.
qs.why: A sofa is a piece of furniture.

qs.q: Match each room to its use
Put the words in order

Challenge: complete: The pen is ___ the box. (inside)
Challenge: complete: You sleep on a ___. (furniture)

learn.b: What asks about things: What is this? Who asks about people: Who is she? Where asks about places: Where do you live?
When asks about time: When is the class? Why asks for a reason: Why are you sad? How asks about the way: How are you? How old are you?
Use Do or Does at the start: Do you like pizza? Does she play football? Answer Yes, I do or No, she doesn't.

qs.q: Which word asks about a person?
Choose the correct question.
Choose the correct question.

Does she play football? is a correct question.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: ___ old are you?
lab.why: How old are you? asks age.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: ___ do you live? (asks about a place)
lab.hint: It starts with wh and asks about place.

learn.b: A shirt, trousers, a dress, shoes, a hat and a coat are clothes. You wear shoes on your feet and a hat on your head.
Sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy and snowy describe the weather. Ask What's the weather like? Answer It's sunny.
We use wear for clothes: I wear a coat when it is cold. Say It's raining for rain happening now.

qs.q: What do you wear on your feet?
What is a good answer to 'What's the weather like?'
qs.why: Weather answers use words like sunny.

qs.q: When it is cold, you wear...
Which word describes weather with water falling from clouds?
You wear a hat on your feet.
qs.why: You wear a hat on your head.

qs.q: Match each word to its meaning
Put the words in order

lab.q: Challenge: complete: You wear ___ on your feet.
lab.why: You wear shoes on your feet.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: It's cold, so I wear a ___.
Challenge: complete: When water falls from clouds, the weather is ___.

learn.b: Use am, is or are plus a verb with -ing. I am reading. She is playing. They are eating.
Most verbs just add -ing: play, playing. If a verb ends in -e, drop it: make, making. Short verbs double the last letter: run, running.
Add not after am, is or are: He is not sleeping. For questions, swap the order: Are you working? Yes, I am.

qs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She is reading a book now.
She is read a book now.
She are reading a book now.

qs.q: What is the -ing form of 'run'?
What is the -ing form of 'make'?
Choose the correct question.
They are play football is correct.
qs.why: The correct sentence is They are playing football.

qs.q: Match each verb to its -ing form
Put the words in order

lab.q: Challenge: complete: She is ___ lunch now. (eat)
lab.why: Is plus eating is present continuous.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: They ___ playing football. (be)
Challenge: write the -ing form of 'run'.

learn.b: For regular verbs, add ed to talk about the past. Play becomes played and walk becomes walked. We often use words like yesterday and last week.
Some common verbs change form. Go becomes went, eat becomes ate, see becomes saw, and have becomes had. You need to learn these.
Use didn't plus the base verb. I didn't go to school. Do not add ed after didn't.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: Yesterday I ___ pizza.
qs.why: Ate is the past simple of eat.

qs.q: What is the past simple of 'go'?
qs.why: Go is irregular, and its past simple is went.

qs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
qs.why: After didn't, use the base verb: come.

qs.q: What is the past simple of 'play'?
'I goed to the park' is correct English.
qs.why: The correct form is 'I went to the park.'

qs.q: Match each verb to its past form
Put these times in order from earliest to latest

lab.q: Challenge: write the past simple of 'go'.
Challenge: write the past simple of 'buy'.
Challenge: write the past simple of 'have'.

learn.b: Use have or has plus the past participle. I have seen that film. She has finished. Irregular participles: go-gone, see-seen, eat-eaten, do-done, write-written.
Use the present perfect for experiences without a time: I have been to Paris. Have you ever eaten sushi? I have never flown.
Just means a short time ago, already means earlier than expected and yet is for negatives and questions. For is a length of time (for two years). Since is a starting point (since 2020).

qs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She finished her homework yesterday ago.
qs.why: Use has plus the past participle.

qs.q: What is the past participle of 'write'?
Choose the correct word: 'I have lived here ___ 2019.'
qs.why: Since goes with a starting point.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: 'I have lived here ___ five years.'
qs.why: For goes with a length of time.

qs.q: 'Have you ever eaten sushi?' asks about life experience.
qs.why: Ever with the present perfect asks about experience.

qs.q: Match each verb to its past participle
Put the words in order

lab.q: Challenge: write the past participle of 'see'.
lab.why: The past participle of see is seen.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: She has ___ here for five years. (live)
Challenge: complete: I ___ never eaten sushi.
lab.why: I have never eaten is correct.

learn.b: Use was or were plus the -ing form. I was sleeping. They were playing. Use was with I, he, she, it and were with you, we, they.
The past continuous shows what was happening at a moment: At 8 pm I was watching TV. It was raining all day.
Use while with the long action and when with the short one: I was cooking when the phone rang. While I was cooking, he was reading.

qs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the correct sentence.
o: I was read when she called.
I was reading when she called.
I were reading when she called.

qs.q: Which action was the longer one? 'I was cooking when the phone rang.'
qs.why: The past continuous shows the longer action.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: '___ I was walking, it started to rain.'
qs.why: While goes with a long action.

qs.q: We use 'were' with 'I' in the past continuous.

Put the words in order

lab.q: Challenge: complete: They ___ playing football at five. (was or were)
Challenge: complete: I ___ reading when the phone rang. (was or were)
Challenge: complete: She was ___ dinner. (cook)

learn.b: Say Turn left or Turn right. Say Go straight to keep walking forward. Say Stop at the corner when you must stop.
Next to means beside. Opposite means on the other side. Between means in the middle of two things. Near means close and far means a long way away.
Start with Excuse me. Then ask Where is the bank? or How do I get to the station? These questions are polite and clear.

qs.q: Which word is the opposite of 'left'?
qs.why: Left and right are opposite directions.

qs.q: Which question asks for directions politely?
o: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
qs.why: It uses Excuse me and a full question.

qs.q: 'The bank is next to the post office' means the bank is ...
What does 'Go straight' mean?
qs.why: Go straight means keep going forward.

qs.q: 'Far' means a short distance away.
qs.why: Far means a long distance away. Near means a short distance.

qs.q: Match each phrase to its meaning
pairs: In the middle of two things

qs.q: Put the words in order to make a question

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Turn ___ at the corner. (opposite of right)
lab.why: Left is the opposite of right.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Go ___ ahead and do not turn. (one word)
lab.why: Go straight ahead means do not turn.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Could you tell me ___ the station is?

learn.b: A passport lets you travel to other countries. A ticket lets you take a train or plane. An airport is where planes land. A hotel is where you sleep on a trip.
Ask How much is this? to learn the price. Expensive means it costs a lot. Cheap means it costs little. A receipt is paper that shows what you paid.
Say I'd like to buy this, please. Say I'd like to book a room for two nights. You can also ask Can I pay by card?

qs.q: Which word means 'costs a lot of money'?
qs.why: Expensive means it costs a lot.

qs.q: You show this at the airport to travel to another country.
qs.why: A passport proves who you are when you travel abroad.

qs.q: How do you ask the price of something?
qs.why: How much is this? asks about the price.

qs.q: Where do you sleep when you travel?
qs.why: A hotel is a place to sleep on a trip.

qs.q: 'Cheap' means something costs a lot.
qs.why: Cheap means it costs very little.

qs.q: Match each word to its meaning
Put the words in order to make a question

lab.q: Challenge: complete: How ___ is this jacket? (asks the price)
Challenge: complete: You need a ___ to fly to another country.
lab.why: A passport is needed to travel abroad.

lab.q: Challenge: write the word for the money you get back when you pay too much.
lab.why: Change is the money you get back.

learn.b: Add -er to short adjectives: tall, taller. Use more with long adjectives: more interesting. Then use than: My brother is taller than me.
Add -est to short adjectives: the tallest. Use the most with long adjectives: the most expensive. Say the best city in the world.
Good, better, best. Bad, worse, worst. Use as ... as for equal things: She is as tall as me.

qs.q: What is the comparative of 'big'?
Choose the correct sentence.
o: This book is interestinger than that one.
This book is more interesting than that one.
This book is most interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting that that one.
qs.why: Use more plus than for long adjectives.

qs.q: What is the superlative of 'bad'?
Choose the correct sentence.
o: She is as taller as me.
She is more tall as me.
She is as tall than me.
She is as tall as me.
qs.why: Use as ... as with the basic adjective.

qs.q: The superlative of 'good' is 'goodest'.
qs.why: The superlative of good is best.

qs.q: Match each adjective to its comparative
Put the words in order

lab.q: Challenge: write the comparative of 'good'.
Challenge: write the comparative of 'big'.
Challenge: write the superlative of 'expensive' with 'the'.

learn.b: A headache is pain in your head. A cold, a cough, a fever and a sore throat are common problems. Ask What's the matter? Answer I have a headache.
Use should plus the base verb. You should see a doctor. You shouldn't eat so much sugar. Should I take this medicine?
A doctor works in a hospital or surgery. A pharmacy sells medicine. A prescription is a paper from the doctor for medicine.

qs.q: Choose the correct advice.
o: You should to drink more water.
qs.why: Use should plus the base verb.

qs.q: What does 'sore throat' mean?
Where can you buy medicine?
Which question asks about a health problem?
qs.why: What's the matter? asks about a problem.

qs.q: A prescription is a paper from the doctor for medicine.
Match each problem to its meaning
Put the words in order

lab.q: Challenge: complete: You ___ drink more water. (advice)
Challenge: write the word for pain in your head.
lab.why: A headache is pain in the head.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: I have a sore ___. (it hurts when you swallow)

learn.b: A nurse, an engineer, a lawyer, a chef and a mechanic are jobs. A chef cooks in a restaurant. A mechanic repairs cars.

A boss is the person in charge. A colleague is a person you work with. A salary is the money you get each month. You apply for a job and go to an interview.

learn.b: Start with I think, I believe, or In my opinion. Say I agree if you think the same. Say I disagree if you think differently.
Because gives a reason. But shows a contrast. So shows a result. For example: I was tired, so I went to bed.
Use am, is, or are going to plus a verb for a plan: I am going to travel next year. Use more before long adjectives: more interesting. Use er for short ones: bigger.

qs.why: To agree is to think the same as someone.

learn.b: Use going to for plans: I'm going to study tonight. Use will for quick decisions and predictions: I'll help you. It will rain tomorrow.
Use if plus the present simple, then will plus a base verb. If it rains, we will stay home. This talks about real future possibilities.
Unless means if not. Unless you hurry, you will be late. Negative: If you don't study, you won't pass.

qs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: If it rains, we will stay at home.
If it will rain, we will stay at home.
If it rains, we stay will at home.
If it rained, we will stay at home.
qs.why: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

qs.q: Which sentence talks about a plan?
o: I'm going to visit my aunt.
If I see her, I will say hello.
qs.why: Going to is used for plans.

qs.q: What does 'unless' mean?
Choose the correct sentence.
o: If you won't study, you don't pass.
If you don't study, you don't pass.
If you didn't study, you won't pass.
If you don't study, you won't pass.
qs.why: Use present simple in the if part.

qs.q: In the first conditional, we use 'will' in the if part.
qs.why: The if part uses the present simple.
